title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 64-66). Grothendieck is building an axiomatic 'analysis situs' of figures, axioms At 1 to At 11. A figure F has a finite poset F~ of 'atoms' or cells (elements of M). Two relations are in play: G <= F means G is a sub-figure, i.e. a down-closed subset of F~. F' << F means F' is contained in F (inclusion, not necessarily cellular). A third relation X' <<° X between atoms reads 'interior of X' contained in interior of X'. For an atom Z << F, the set F~^Z = {X in F~ | Z << X} is expected to have a smallest element.

Proposition (p. 64). Let F' << F and G <= F. Then Inf^{<<}(F', G) exists and equals the sub-figure G' of F' with G'~ = {X' in F'~ | X' << G}.

On p. 64 it is shown that this set is down-closed, hence a sub-figure of F' with G' << F and G' << G.

This page proves the universal property: for any figure Phi, (Phi << F' and Phi << G) implies Phi << G'.
- By At 4 (a figure is << H iff each of its atoms is, and an atom << H lies in some atom of H), reduce to Phi = Z an atom.
- Let X' be the smallest element of F'~^Z. Then Z <<° X'.
- It suffices to show X' is in G'~, i.e. X' << G.

Lemma. Suppose F' << F, G <= F, X' in F'~, Z <<° X' and Z << G. Then X' << G.

Proof of the lemma.
- Let X be the unique atom of F with X' <<° X (existence and uniqueness come from F' << F).
- By At 7 (transitivity of <<°), Z <<° X, so X is the smallest element of F~^Z.
- Since Z << G, At 4 gives Y in G~ with Z << Y. Since G~ is contained in F~, Y lies in F~^Z, so X <= Y by minimality.
- Hence X' << X <= Y <= G, so X' << G. QED.

In modern terms: inside a 'tame' cell-stratified setting (regular CW or polyhedral complexes, o-minimal cell decompositions), the meet of a closed subset F' and a subcomplex G, taken in the lattice of figures ordered by inclusion, is the subcomplex of F' made of the cells of F' lying in G. Equivalently it is the preimage of G~ under the 'carrier' map phi: F'~ -> F~, X' maps to the unique X with X' <<° X. Page 66 exploits exactly this. Corollary 1: if F' <= F, then G' = F' ∧ G. Corollary 2: G maps to F'.G = phi^{-1}(G~), which commutes with Sup and Inf. This is a preparatory step toward Mayer-Vietoris or descent-type statements for coverings by sub-figures (Corollary 3).
errors: No mathematical error in the argument. One small gap: the reduction uses that the minimal element X' of F'~^Z satisfies Z <<° X' (needed to apply the Lemma). This is not stated on the page and must come from an axiom (presumably At 7 or the carrier axioms, the analogue of 'the closed cell of the carrier of int Z is the smallest closed cell containing Z'). Also, 'X' << X' in the final chain uses that <<° implies <<, which is implicit.

ideas.what: Intersection of a closed figure with a subcomplex, computed as the set of cells of F' lying in G, and proved to be the infimum for inclusion.
ideas.modern_name: Restriction or pullback of a subcomplex along the carrier map of a subdivision / closed subset in a regular cell complex (o-minimal cell decomposition compatibility)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL and CW topology (Whitehead, Zeeman, Hudson); o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight-Pillay-Steinhorn, 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic call for 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the axiomatics At 1 to At 11 appear unpublished.

ideas.what: Carrier map phi: F'~ -> F~ (unique X with X' <<° X) and the identification of G maps to F'.G with phi^{-1} on down-closed subsets.
ideas.modern_name: Carrier / poset map between face posets; inverse image of lower sets (exit-path / Alexandrov-topology viewpoint)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard combinatorial topology; the stratified-poset viewpoint is associated with MacPherson, Treumann and Lurie (exit paths)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA; possibly echoed in the stratified-structure ideas of Esquisse d'un programme §5-6

missed.claim: The page is a routine lemma inside an unpublished axiomatic system ('At 1'-'At 11', axiomes de liaison) for tame figures given by a poset of atoms, the relations << and <<°, and a sub-figure lattice. This is an attempt at an axiomatic tame topology, distinct from o-minimality, that was never published. The system as a whole, rather than this lemma, is the potentially unrecorded item.
missed.quote: Alors par At 7 on a Z <<° X donc X est le plus petit élément de F~^Z
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a cell-poset-based axiomatics for tame geometry, comparable to o-minimal structures and to stratified spaces with exit-path posets. A historian could compare it with the 'topologie modérée' program of the Esquisse; on its own this page adds little.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, elementary lattice-theoretic lemma (meet of a closed figure with a subcomplex equals the cellular preimage). It is interesting only as evidence of Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatisation of tame topology, not as a new result.
